extracted.intended_audience: researchers seeking funding from Alzheimer's Research UK (dementia researchers)
extracted.subtask_description: Overview of Alzheimer's Research UK's funding priorities, schemes, and resources for researchers seeking support in dementia/Alzheimer's research, with emphasis on translational and career-stage-specific funding. Useful as guidance for aligning applications and activities with the charity's strategic aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support biomedical research that will take us closer to treatments
rubrics_metrics.description: Alzheimer's Research UK is committed to supporting biomedical research that will take us closer to treatments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This commitment underpins the charity's funding schemes (Project grants for tenured researchers, PhD Scholarships, Research Fellowships) and indicates a preference for biomedical work with therapeutic relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accelerate the 'bench-to-bedside' journey / rapid translation to patient benefit
rubrics_metrics.description: Our focus is to accelerate the ‘bench-to-bedside’ journey: our funding seeks to translate scientific findings into patient benefit as rapidly as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications and projects that demonstrate clear pathways to clinical or patient impact, and plans to accelerate translation, are aligned with the charity's strategic priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research priority areas: prevention, diagnosis and treatments
rubrics_metrics.description: We have a wide range of funding streams that support work on prevention, diagnosis and treatments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals addressing these domains (prevention, diagnostic approaches, therapeutic development) are within the core scope of supported work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support and opportunities for early career researchers
rubrics_metrics.description: We build capacity through our PhD Scholarships and Research Fellowships and provide resources via an Early Career Researcher Portal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are dedicated schemes and resources intended to support career development; early career applicants should consult these tailored opportunities and resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translational initiatives and platforms (Translational Hub)
rubrics_metrics.description: Translational Hub: Find out about our range of translational initiatives and platforms to help researchers progress their discoveries towards therapeutic application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Researchers with translational projects can leverage hub resources and platforms to advance discoveries toward therapeutic application; use these initiatives to strengthen translational plans in proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouragement of collaborative, networked research
rubrics_metrics.description: The Alzheimer’s Research UK Research Network is a unique, collaborative venture in the dementia research community; Network Centres are highlighted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collaboration and networked approaches are emphasised; projects that leverage or contribute to the Research Network or Network Centres align with the charity's collaborative priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ambitious initiatives targeting urgent, complex research questions (Dementia Frontiers Fund)
rubrics_metrics.description: Dementia Frontiers Fund: Information for researchers — A bold, ambitious initiative empowering researchers to tackle three of the most urgent and complex questions in dementia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highly ambitious proposals that address urgent, complex questions in dementia may be suitable for strategic initiatives like this fund; applicants should align proposals to the stated urgent questions where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring the impact and progress of funded research
rubrics_metrics.description: We monitor the impact and progress of the research that we fund in a number of ways.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funded projects are subject to impact monitoring; applicants should be prepared to define measurable impact and reporting mechanisms in their proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participation in conferences and dissemination/networking activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Research Conference: join UK’s dementia researchers and leading experts for two days of groundbreaking science, inspiring discussions, and invaluable networking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engagement in community events, dissemination and networking is part of the research ecosystem supported by the charity; demonstrating plans for dissemination and community engagement can strengthen an application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility/format signals: multiple scheme types (project grants, scholarships, fellowships)
rubrics_metrics.description: Alzheimer’s Research UK has a large number of different grant schemes through which you can apply for funding; examples include Project grants for tenured researchers, PhD Scholarships and Research Fellowships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should select the scheme matching their career stage and project type; scheme-specific eligibility and expectations (tenure status, career stage, project aims) should be checked on individual scheme pages.
